title: Kobra Release Manifest
description: Companion to game/release.manifest.json (spec Section 12, Appendix B). Identifies a release, indexes its payload for update verification, and declares the save migration chain. The launcher verifies this manifest's hashes before applying an update: verification is mandatory for the release payload, unlike the advisory per-asset hashes (FR-AST-6).

release.description: Date-version release identifier, e.g. 2026.09.1. Ordering is lexicographic on the zero-padded components.

previous_release.description: Release this one supersedes; null for a first release. Used to select the patch archive.

launcher_min.description: FR-UPD-6. Minimum launcher version. A release MUST refuse to run under an older launcher and instruct the user to replace it.

save_version.description: Save format version produced by this release. MUST match engine.manifest.json save_version or the release build fails (FR-SCH-5).

game_version.description: The game's own content version. Independent of engine_version and release (Packaging spec §4.4). Stamped into every save header. Required by the packaging pipeline; optional here only so that a document written before the field existed still validates.

scope.description: full: whole game folder. game-only: game/ subtree for manual over-extraction over an existing install. patch: delta from previous_release.

total_size.description: FR-UPD-5. Declared total extracted size: the sum of every files[].size. The launcher checks the archive against this before extraction begins (zip-bomb defence). NOT the compressed archive size — that is archive.size.

archive.description: The update archive this manifest describes (Packaging spec §8.2.2). Required on a published manifest and enforced by the launcher: internal/update/verify.go refuses a manifest that declares neither archive.hash nor the flat archive_sha256 alias, rather than silently downgrading to per-file verification (§8.2.3.3). The manifest is never a member of the archive it names, which is what makes this hash well defined.

url.description: Absolute, or relative to the manifest's own location.

size.description: Exact compressed archive size in bytes. Not total_size, which is the extracted size.

files.description: File index. Hashes here are MANDATORY to verify during update, unlike asset manifest hashes.

path.description: Relative path. MUST be under game/ or launcher/: a release never contains and never writes data/, which holds the user's saves, config, and mods (FR-UPD-7). The launcher verifies after extraction that nothing touched data/.

mode.description: POSIX mode, used to restore the executable bit on launcher files that pass through archives which do not preserve it (Section 13.3).

migrations.description: Ordered save migration chain (FR-SAVE-12). Each step MUST advance the version (from < to). Full chain contiguity from the oldest supported save_version to save_version cannot be expressed in JSON Schema and MUST be checked by the semantic validator in the release build (FR-SCH-6); a release whose chain has a gap MUST fail the build.

fn.description: Exported migration function name. Runs on a copy of the payload; the original is preserved as prev-<from> before the first post-migration write (FR-SAVE-13).

schema_migrations.description: FR-SCH-4. One-way manifest schema upgrades, e.g. asset-manifest/1 -> /2, with the pre-migration file preserved.

signatures.description: FR-LNCH-3. Optional detached signatures over the manifest itself, so a user who distrusts the transport can verify the release.

allOf.description: A patch release must name its previous release, and its migration chain (if any) must start at save_version.

hash.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 with an algorithm prefix, matching the save, engine and asset schemas. The prefix is required: internal/update/parseHash rejects a bare 64-character hex string, so a publisher who emits unprefixed hex produces a manifest the launcher refuses even though the bytes are correct (Packaging spec §8.2.2).

relPath.description: POSIX-style relative path. No leading slash, no backslash, no empty or dot segments, ASCII-only by policy (FR-I18N-7). The negative lookahead rejects '.' and '..' segments so a crafted manifest cannot escape its root.
